newsitem.title: USA: Quaker seeks to improve Latin America food.
newsitem.headline: Quaker seeks to improve Latin America food.

text.p: Quaker Oats Co Chairman William Smithburg said Wednesday that the company will consider steps to improve its international food operations, particularly in Latin America.
"We need to consider honing the Latin American portfolio," Smithburg told a teleconference Wednesday.
Earlier, Quaker said it planned it may sell some non-core businesses and potentially restructure certain international operations.
Smithburg added that Quaker may also consider partnerships for some international operations, including in Latin America.
Smithburg added that the company remains optimistic about potential in China, where it has met its targets for both cereal and Gatorade sports drink over the past couple of years.
U.S. food profits, which were hurt in the first quarter by last year's reduction in ready-to-eat cereal prices, are expected to improve for the full-year.
"We expect profits in U.S. food to be up this year," Smithburg said.
In the first quarter, U.S. and Canadian food operating income fell to $77.2 million from $99.0 million a year ago.
Smithburg said he also expects better international foods profits, particularly in the second half of the year, as Latin American operations improve.
In the first quarter, Quaker's international foods operating income dropped to $800,000 from $900,000 a year ago.
Earlier, Quaker said it expected to stimulate international profitability by concentrating "almost exclusively" on Quaker and Gatorade brands.
Quaker also said it expects to take restructuring charges in the range of $50 million to $100 million pretax before year-end.

Smithburg said Quaker has identified about $20 million of overhead costs associated with its Snapple beverage business, which it has agreed to sell. The company also hopes to eliminate about $30 million in other costs.

The company took a first-quarter $1.14 billion after-tax loss on the pending sale of Snapple, which operated at a loss for the two years that Quaker owned it. Earlier, Quaker reported income excluding the Snapple loss of $0.24 a share, up from $0.22 a year ago before a $0.01 gain.
Regarding the chief executive succesion plan that was announced today, Smithburg said a search for candidates began this week both inside and outside the company.
"(Quaker is) casting a very wide net to get the best range of candidates we can," Smithburg added.
He said the search for a chief executive likely will take "a matter of months," adding he expects to work with the new person through a transition period.
"Then I plan on retiring," he added. "This is not a long-term thing."
Smithburg, whose age in the 1996 annual report is listed as 58, said he will give up both the chief executive and chairman titles. He has held both for about 16 years.
Quaker shares rose 5/8 to 38-7/8.
